GitHub Issue:
Post Date: 2019-07-08T18:42:57Z
Current Date: April 4 2025
Title: Double.TryParse succeeds and returns an incorrect value for strings in scientific notation that exceed the bounds of a double.
Description: .NET Core Version: Version: 3.0.100-preview6-012264 - I think. VS2019 apparently hides the NetCore packages, now, so I am not 100% sure. 
Have you experienced this same bug with .NET Framework?: No

Run the following code: 
            var text = "123e466";
            var provider = new CultureInfo("en-US");
            double value;

            var success = Double.TryParse(
                text,
                NumberStyles.Any & ~NumberStyles.AllowTrailingSign,
                provider,
                out value);

            MessageBox.Show(this, value.ToString(), success.ToString());

Results in DotNetFramework: 
	success = false
	value = 0

Results in NetCore:
	success = true
	value = double.Infinity

It seems to me that the original .Net Framework results were correct. "123e466" exceeds the bounds of a double, but it should fail to parse, not return Infinity.
